paper_id: Frequency Matching in Spiking Neural Networks for mmWave Sensing
title: Frequency Matching in Spiking Neural Networks for mmWave Sensing
motivation: mmWave sensing on edge devices suffers tension between accuracy and efficiency; existing ANN pipelines require heavy preprocessing or deep architectures
problem_framing: Mechanism-data alignment: characterize how LIF neuron low-pass dynamics interact with mmWave signal spectral structure
key_insight: LIF dynamics act as implicit low-pass filter; matching effective bandwidth to discriminative spectral content of mmWave signals enables inherent noise suppression
method_signature: Frequency-matching criterion for configuring membrane decay factor β by aligning LIF effective bandwidth with discriminative spectrum
evaluation_criteria: Test accuracy improvement and theoretical energy consumption reduction vs ANN baselines across four mmWave datasets
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Maximum-deviation rule marks onset of over-low-pass behavior; beyond this point further low-pass bias yields diminishing discriminative spectrum retention
evidence_for_taste: clarifying when and why SNNs outperform ANNs
accuracy-agnostic method to identify reference boundary
thinking_moves: 把感知问题重新形式化为频域机制-数据对齐问题
建立LIF动力学与IIR低通滤波器的等价性连接
从数据频谱结构出发定义判别性频带而非预设先验
用几何偏差而非性能指标确定参数边界
